To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
degenerative aging is a treatable medical condition that is not a natural process of life and is not a normal process of life.

the degenerative aging process can be defined as a treatable medical condition and that its definition is important for the development of therapies and for the compliance with national and international program requirements.

the aging of humans is a complex and heterogeneous process that can be described as a combination of a number of different processes, each of which is associated with a different set of symptoms and different risk factors, but that can be described in a simple way as the accumulation of damage to cells and tissues.

the development of generally agreed definitions and diagnostic criteria for the multifaceted degenerative aging process, and for the effectiveness and safety of interventions against it, as well as with their potential implementation in national and international health programs and regulatory frameworks.
